label: Class-IV refinement I
title: Generic 2D soup is not a simple continuation of the ECA phenotype
summary: A dimension-neutral persistence × spreading surrogate keeps the ECA controls but does not place Life, HighLife and Day & Night in one stable quadrant across densities. The exact HighLife width-one = Rule 54 bridge shows the retention statistic is observer-relative while history gain and spreading transport exactly; height-one strips forget twelve of eighteen Life-like rule bits and height two recovers all of them.
takeaway: Selective retention is a statistic of dynamics, observation map and reference ensemble together; a lower-dimensional presentation can be an exact quotient that hides rule distinctions.

label: Class-IV refinement II
title: When added transverse freedom reveals and changes a Life-like rule
summary: On periodic strips of height 1 to 16, persistence and spreading are strongly non-monotone in height and ensemble-sensitive; Life and B35/S236 are the same rule at height one and diverge after one update at height two; the selective-surprisal gap decomposes exactly into a coarse-visible term and a within-fiber residual.
takeaway: Strip height behaves like a representation scale, not a complexity knob; distinctions erased by a quotient can be kept as residual coordinates.

promotion.idea: A one-dimensional shadow can hide most of a two-dimensional rule

label: Class-IV refinement III
title: Jev as a semantic feature scout for the 54/110 phenotype
summary: Shown anonymous primitive measurements of 88 ECA representatives, Jev's persistence-across-conditions and selective-memory judgements rank 54 and 110 with AUC 1.0 against Class III and only Class-II confounders; an opaque control does not reproduce this. The matched codebook ablation reproduces J1, J3 and J5 with operational definitions alone and weakens J4.
takeaway: A judgement model can point at a mechanism worth distilling; the science then lives in the transparent statistic, not in the model.

label: Class-IV refinement IV
title: Selective predictive persistence × spreading: the recovered discriminator record
kind: Record of a prospective finite result with partial provenance
summary: S = max(0,R)·max(0,M) with S > 0.20 and α_512 > 0.50, frozen before fresh simulation, selects 54/110 in 10/10 decisions and 0/420 undisputed negatives across five fresh conditions, rejecting 41/106 and a radius-two rare-correction adversary. The report and tables survive; the protocol, runner and canonical JSON bytes do not.
takeaway: A finite discriminator for the 54/110 core phenotype, not a Wolfram-class classifier, and recorded at the provenance level it can support.

label: Class-IV refinement V
title: The height-one fiber of Rule 54 is enriched in the persistence × spreading phenotype
summary: Sampling 512 Life-like rules from each height-one fiber of ECAs 54, 22, 90, 204 and 0 and measuring at height two, the both-positive fraction is 0.47, 0.37, 0.25, 0.22 and 0.07. Fibers differ, fiber(54) is enriched, HighLife and Life are typical members of their fibers; the bet that fiber(22) splits into Life-like and explosive halves failed (72% ballistic).
takeaway: Under one fixed contract a source rule predicts the phenotype distribution of its refinements; whether that is more than the activity its six fixed bits impose is the next control.

label: Class-IV refinement VI
title: The fiber phenotype is not additive in the six exposed bits
summary: All 64 height-one fibers, 128 rules each, at height two: a logistic model with pairwise interactions between the six exposed bits predicts both-positive and spreading fractions better out of sample than main effects alone (LRT p ~ 1e-33; LOO 0.527 vs 0.534), with birth-survival pairs as the strongest terms; persistence is additive out of sample. The affine bases are not special; the 0/90 ordering did not replicate.
takeaway: On the spreading axis the base rule acts as a whole on its refinements; on the persistence axis its bits act independently.

label: Class-IV refinement VII
title: Rule 110 gets a fiber, and it is enriched; chirality is not detectable
summary: A handed family (centre, west neighbour, count of the other seven) whose height-one restriction is a coordinate projection onto all 256 ECAs, every fiber 2^24 rules, so 110 finally has one. Panel of nine fibers at 256 rules each plus all 256 fibers at twelve: fiber(110) is both-positive at 0.543, tied at the top with its mirror 124 and with 54, and far above 30 (0.273). The enrichment is on the persistence axis, not spreading: fibers 22 and 30 spread more and still fall far below. A base's own 1D phenotype predicts its fiber's on both axes across all 256 bases. The mirror fiber 124 is indistinguishable from 110, so chirality is not detectable. The null-pair calibration rejected by chance and was itself mis-designed; a matched-seed control shows the implementation is exactly complement-covariant to 1e-15.
takeaway: The height-one quotient at 110 predicts enrichment of its preimages, and marking a direction changes which rules are in a fiber without changing what the fiber is like.

label: Class-IV refinement VIII
title: The base sets history gain, the completion sets retention
summary: Persistence decomposes into retention and history gain, and a matched grid separates them. Because the height-one restriction is a coordinate projection, a completion is one object shared by every fiber, so the base can be varied with the completion and every seed held fixed. Eight bases x 512 completions: history gain is base-dominated (variance component 0.040 against 0.012) and retention completion-dominated (0.022 against 0.035); holding the completion fixed, 110 beats 30 on history gain for 87% of completions with a null retention difference. History gain anticorrelates between distant bases (Spearman -0.414 for 110 against 30) rather than merely failing to transfer, and no linear model on the 24 completion bits predicts it at all. At height four the persistence-only control overtakes 110, so history-gain inheritance tracks 1D history gain rather than Class-IV-ness.
takeaway: The source rule confers history gain and the refinement chooses its own retention; the conferral is visible in the base's one-dimensional history gain, not in its class.
